title: Staccato: smaller PRs, less Git housekeeping
brief: I want to demo staccato to my coworkers to show them the key workflows where it can save them time if they move to a git stacking workflow.

scenes.notes:
- Familiar pain: large reviews or waiting for a dependency to merge
- One order feature, three independently reviewable changes
- Keep building on unmerged work; Staccato handles branch relationships
scenes.shows: A diagram comparing one large order-feature PR with three stacked PRs: API, validation, UI

scenes.notes:
- st new starts from trunk; st append builds on the current branch
- Commit with Git as usual: one reviewable change per branch
- st log makes the parent relationships visible
- Less branch setup and less remembering what depends on what
scenes.shows: A terminal using st new feature/api, st append feature/validation, st append feature/ui and st log, with normal Git commits between branches

scenes.notes:
- st sync pushes the stack; st sync --down fetches and updates the stack without pushing; st pr make targets each branch's parent
- API targets trunk, validation targets API, UI targets validation
- Smaller diffs for reviewers; continue working on the upper branches
- Requires origin and authenticated GitHub CLI for PR creation
scenes.shows: A terminal pushing with st sync and creating PRs bottom-up with st pr make, beside the three PR base/head relationships

scenes.notes:
- Feedback arrives on the API while UI work already depends on it
- st modify --all stages changes, amends the last commit and restacks branches above
- Replaces the manual checkout-and-rebase loop; returns to the modified branch
- For a new commit instead: git commit, st top, st restack
scenes.shows: A terminal navigating down to feature/api, applying review feedback with st modify --all, then showing the updated three-branch stack

scenes.notes:
- Git rebase conflicts still need resolution: by you or an appropriately equipped agent
- Resolve and stage files, then st continue resumes the stack operation
- st abort restores the pre-operation branches from automatic restack backups
- Commit or stash unrelated changes before rewriting branches
scenes.shows: A short conflict terminal sequence: resolve files, git add, st continue; a small callout for st abort

scenes.notes:
- Bottom PR merges while the rest of the feature is still in progress
- st sync fetches, updates trunk, removes detected merged branches, restacks and pushes
- Less deleting branches, re-parenting children and rebasing by hand
- Force-with-lease for rewritten branches; after a conflict, continue then sync again to push
scenes.shows: Before/after stack diagrams and a terminal running st sync after the API PR merges, leaving validation and UI above updated trunk

scenes.notes:
- A passing top branch does not prove every smaller PR passes
- st exec checks each branch in the current lineage, bottom-up
- One pass/fail report; returns to the starting branch
- Clean tracked files first; choose the team's actual test command
scenes.shows: A terminal running st exec "go test ./..." with a per-branch result report and the original checkout restored

terminal.title: Check the remaining branches • report stdout, live test stderr omitted

steps.output:
Ran on 2 branch(es): go test ./...
  ✔ feature/validation  passed  0.1s
  ✔ feature/ui          passed  0.1s
2 passed, 0 failed

scenes.chapter: Turn a big branch into a stack
scenes.notes:
- Already have a large branch? Split it instead of rebuilding the work by hand
- Give an agent st split describe output; choose reviewable seams together, by commits, paths or intermediate file overrides
- Inspect its JSON plan; preview with st split apply plan.json --dry-run, then apply with --exec to check every slice
- Each slice builds on the previous one; the top slice preserves the original content and branches above stay attached
scenes.shows: A large order-feature branch becoming API, validation and UI slices: a terminal inventory from st split describe, an agent-assisted JSON plan, dry-run preview, and st split apply plan.json --exec "go test ./..."

scenes.notes:
- Try one feature split into two or three dependent PRs
- Keep ordinary Git commits; use Staccato for stack housekeeping
- Existing work can join with st attach <branch> --parent <parent>
- Payoff: smaller reviews, fewer repeated Git steps, less waiting
scenes.shows: A closing card with the lifecycle new → append → modify → sync, and st attach as the entry point for existing branches
